METHODOLOGY / COHERENCE REVIEW (round 3).

The IRIS optimization loop has two locked halves: MEASURE (a 3-layer eval, DL-0022) and EXPLORE (a candidate-generator that emits a ranked top-5 with confounder cards, DL-0023). This is the THIRD piece: M3 — the loop-driver that assembles the generator output into a morning report, gates it on human approval, routes approved items, and persists loop state across runs.

PROPOSAL:
IRIS optimization loop — M3 LOOP-DRIVER + MORNING REPORT + ROUTING + STATE, v1 (r3 FINAL). Measure=DL-0022; explore=DL-0023; top-5 cap=DL-0020; portable loop=DL-0021. Loop lives in dotdev; SUT is IRIS (classdojo/iris). [tunable]=build constant; OPEN=human-input non-blocking.

PURPOSE: assemble the generator's ranked top-5 into a morning report, gate on genuine human approval, route approved items to real targets, persist loop state across runs. v1 manual; auto mode deferred.

A. STATE: committed JSON loop/state.json on a dedicated `loop-state` branch in dotdev (NOT main — DL-0011 blocks main pushes; loop-state exempt from main-protection; a first-run preflight `gh api repos/johnalexwelch/dotdev/rulesets` confirms the exemption). Tracks: baseline pointer {pinned IRIS commit, judge model, capture date, per-case pass map, P10 floor, permutation null}; per-case quarantine clocks; approved-not-yet-landed; landed ledger {id, type, diff hash, approval ts, landed ts, merge entry {repo, sha}, human_edited:bool immutable}; change-counter; sentinel net time-series; suite version; fixture-gap pointer. Read→append→commit each run. Validate schema + SHA-256 checksum of canonicalized JSON; REFUSE malformed/mismatched state. Hand-edits via `loop state edit` (validate + rehash; BLOCKS changes to human_edited on existing entries) or `loop state rehash`. v1 SINGLE-OPERATOR + single-machine file lock (distributed lock deferred).

B. RUN / IDEMPOTENCY: manual `loop run`, keyed {suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit + date}. Lifecycle started → issue_posted:{url} → routed:{ids, pr_urls} → emitted. Same-key re-run idempotent; a crashed run resumes via the §E crash-resume probe. Quarantine clocks advance ONLY at emitted.

C. REPORT (read-only, NOT approval surface): loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md + a dotdev issue (label loop-report). (1) HEADER — date, IRIS commit, baseline freshness + changes-since-baseline, judge model, suite version, counts, budget. (2) LOOP-HEALTH — sentinel net vs prior run (PASS/HALT), generator≠judge; on FAILURE emit ONLY health + zero candidates (precedes candidate processing; no --force/--skip-health). (3) TOP-5 (net desc) — rank, net, type+blast, hypothesis, rendered diff, target cluster, full confounder card (cluster N, holdout N, permutation p, FDR q, cross-lane note, SOLE-DOMAIN + flags), fully-resolved route path (if OD-1/2/3 unresolved render [ROUTE-UNRESOLVED: <OD-N> pending — approval recorded, routing cannot execute]); HIGH-blast/cross-lane as a distinct callout above the approval commands. (4) CANNOT-VALIDATE (separate, below the 5; informational; NOT `loop approve`-eligible in v1; author a fixture if real else `loop reject`). (5) FIXTURE-GAP queue status (count, oldest age, backlog-halt). (6) BLIND-SPOT lines — metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE count + examples; budget-exceeded clusters. (7) STALENESS ALERT — 'N candidates approved >30d have not landed; `loop status`.' (8) CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner — if unresolved, list suspect batch + instructions; persists every report until rollback OR `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + rationale. (9) FOOTER — loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>; 'pending approvals expire when the next loop run completes reconcile.'

D. APPROVAL GATE (CLI, per-candidate): `loop approve <date> <id>` writes {authenticated operator identity, ts, exact diff hash}; fails APPROVAL-DEADLINE-EXPIRED if a newer run key exists. `loop reject <date> <id>` writes explicit rejection (also valid to close a stale approved-not-yet-landed entry). `loop edit <date> <id>` opens the diff in $EDITOR; on save validate + rehash, write {original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}, then REQUIRE a separate `loop approve`. DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by deadline = NOT routed (no rubber-stamp by omission, no batch-approve, no --auto-approve in v1). ROUTING DEADLINE: a candidate is implicitly rejected when the NEXT `loop run` completes reconcile (aligns with daily cadence; cannot approve after a new run starts).

E. ROUTING (approved → target; one artifact per candidate, never batched; two-phase): write status=routing, routing_id=<id> BEFORE any creation. CRASH-RESUME PROBE on resume: `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo <target> --json url --state open`; if found, record URL + continue without recreating; else create. PATH-EXISTENCE VALIDATION for Types 1/2/3: `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<resolved-path>?ref=<iris-commit>`; if missing, abort ROUTE-TARGET-STALE before two-phase. Write the artifact URL to state before advancing. Type 1 prompt/instruction → PR into classdojo/iris at the path from loop/config/iris-prompt-targets.yaml ({sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→paths), branch loop/<date>-<id>, body = hypothesis + confounder card + report link + [HUMAN-EDITED] if applicable. Type 2 reflection/habit → PR into iris (v1 PR-only, no direct store write), scoped {scope, scope_key}, path from iris-habit-targets.yaml (OD-2 must resolve first, else ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2). Type 3 tool schema/description → PR into iris at the path from iris-tool-targets.yaml; REQUIRES a {target_tool_path} field on the candidate. Type 4 retrieval-corpus → NOT auto-PR'd; human-judgment ISSUE in classdojo/iris (EVAL-INVISIBLE). Type 5 routing/findings-pipeline code → ISSUE into classdojo/iris (needs implementation), triage-labeled. Fixture-gap note → ISSUE in classdojo/iris (fixtures live at backend/src/iris/eval/), label fixture-audit, links to the dotdev report. Every artifact carries candidate id + report link + confounder card + [HUMAN-EDITED] marker, links back to the ledger.

F. LANDED → LEDGER → BASELINE: `loop reconcile` runs automatically as the FIRST step of every run. Queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix loop/ AND base:default-branch. Per newly-merged PR: extract candidate id from the branch, verify merge {repo, sha} not already in the ledger (dedup on BOTH repo AND sha), secondary duplicate-candidate-id check (surface a conflict warning rather than silently increment), mark landed, increment change-counter. 'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch (loop approve = human-approval event; GitHub merge = landing event; no second approval). At change-counter=[5 tunable] OR a judge/IRIS model bump, PROPOSE a baseline refresh (never auto); human confirms → capture records a new baseline pointer + resets quarantine clocks + re-quarantines the pre-refresh holdout set (DL-0023 §E).

G. PROVENANCE: at each refresh, the DL-0023 §J delta-vs-last-baseline check attributes per-case regressions to the batch of ≤5 landed candidates since the last refresh (batch granularity, known limitation); human-edited candidates included with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag. A newly-regressed case raises CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION + surfaces the suspect batch for a human rollback decision (revert the suspect iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture). CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persists in the LOOP-HEALTH banner until rollback OR `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + written rationale (dismissal ≠ rollback).

H. SECRETS / ACCESS: scoring needs warehouse creds + LLM keys (--execute --e2e). v1 operator local creds from env/secret store; keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs. Preflight verifies write access to classdojo/iris (branch + PR + issue) BEFORE scoring; failure aborts with a credential error ('preflight failed: {service}', no usernames/hostnames/warehouse names). Secret-pattern scrubbing (sk-*, AKIA*, connection strings) on all LLM outputs before report/PR. [OPEN: local vs CI runner].

I. AUTO MODE (deferred, slice 6): v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path until a multi-run track record + trusted sentinel/health.

J. RECOVERY RUNBOOK — LOOP PR FAILS IRIS CI: run `loop reject <date> <id>` (writes explicit rejection, clears the approved-not-yet-landed entry, lets the next run's generator re-cluster from the same failure class if it persists). Do NOT hand-push fixes to the loop/ branch — reject and let the generator re-propose with corrected cluster evidence.

OPEN DECISIONS (human input, non-blocking for design; blocking for their route type at runtime): OD-1 iris prompt file paths; OD-2 habit/reflection store path (→ iris-habit-targets.yaml before Type 2 routing); OD-3 iris branch-protection effect on loop/ PRs (→ §J runbook); OD-4 local vs CI runner.

Generator emits 3 validated; sentinel PASS. #1 engagement-attribution habit (net 3, MEDIUM, [SOLE-DOMAIN]) → `loop approve 2026-08-01 1` → path-existence check passes → two-phase route → PR to iris at the resolved habit path, branch loop/2026-08-01-1. #2 `loop edit 2026-08-01 2` then `loop approve 2026-08-01 2` → routed [HUMAN-EDITED] (excluded from net-attribution, flagged in regression-attribution). #3 `loop reject 2026-08-01 3` or no action by deadline. ## Critique

**Summary:** The proposal is substantially sound — all 14 round-2 fixes check out, and the core state, idempotency, and attribution mechanics are coherent. Two concrete design contradictions need resolution before implementation can safely start.

---

### Lens 1 — STATE MODEL

**AGREE, with one minor flag.**

- Single source of truth (loop/state.json on loop-state), SHA-256 guard, `REFUSE` on mismatch, and `human_edited` immutable — correct.
- Dedup on `{repo, sha}` with secondary candidate-id warning prevents double-landing.
- Change-counter increments per merged PR; quarantine clocks advance only at `emitted` — these are correctly decoupled.
- Preflight `gh api repos/johnalexwelch/dotdev/rulesets` correctly confirms loop-state is not covered by the DL-0011 main-only ruleset.

**Flag (non-blocking):** Reconcile queries "merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix `loop/`." No `loop/` PRs merge into dotdev's main — all routes go to classdojo/iris (Types 1–3 as PRs; Types 4–5 as issues). The dotdev query is spurious. It adds confusion without risk. Recommend removing it or documenting explicitly why it's there (e.g. future expansion).

---

### Lens 2 — IDEMPOTENCY / CRASH-RESUME

**AGREE for same-day crashes. OBJECT for cross-day crashes.**

Same-key crash-resume is correct: write `status=routing` before creation, probe `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --state open` before recreating, write URL before advancing. Within the same date the scheme is sound.

**Concrete gap:** The run key includes `date`. If a run crashes at `status=routed` and the operator resumes the *next* day, the new date produces a new run key. The new run's reconcile picks up only MERGED PRs with `loop/` prefix — but the prior day's PRs may still be open (approved, created, not yet reviewed/merged). The crash-resume probe is never invoked for the old key. Those open PRs are opaque to the new run: the operator sees them in classdojo/iris but the loop doesn't surface them, track their approval status, or warn about the dangling state. They'll eventually merge and reconcile will pick them up correctly (`{repo, sha}` dedup prevents double-landing), but until then the state shows them as approved-not-yet-landed for the old run and the new run has no visibility that the old run was never emitted.

**Recommended correction (small):** Add a `STALE-RUN` check to the start of every new run: if any run exists in state with `status ≠ emitted` and a run key ≠ today's, surface a warning listing the stale run key and its routed-but-open PR URLs. No action required — just visibility.

---

### Lens 3 — REPORT DECISION-COMPLETENESS

**OBJECT on lifecycle ordering contradiction.**

The report (§C.3) requires "fully-resolved route path" for each candidate — actual PR/issue URLs in classdojo/iris. These URLs only exist after routing completes. But the run lifecycle is: `started → issue_posted:{url} → routed:{ids, pr_urls} → emitted`. The morning report issue is posted *before* routing. This is internally contradictory: you cannot show a fully-resolved route path in a report posted before routing runs.

This is not a nitpick. Different implementers would resolve it differently:
- Post the issue early with placeholder paths, then edit it after routing — adds an implicit "issue edit" step not in the spec.
- Post the issue at `emitted` time (after routing) — consistent with report content, but then `issue_posted` isn't a distinct lifecycle step.
- `issue_posted` refers to a separate tracking/kickoff issue (not the morning report), and the morning report is committed at `emitted` — plausible, but not stated.

**Recommended correction:** Clarify that `issue_posted` in the lifecycle refers to a lightweight run-tracking stub (just "run started, report will be here"), posted early so the operator has a URL to watch. The full morning report (including route paths) is written at `emitted` time — committed to `loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` on loop-state *and* posted as an edit/update to the stub issue, or as a separate issue posted at emit. The spec should state which.

All other report content checks pass: header, sentinel PASS/HALT, confounder card per candidate (permutation p, FDR q, blast tier, cross-lane note, flags), HIGH-blast callout, CANNOT-VALIDATE separation, fixture-gap backlog status, staleness alert, cumulative-regression banner, footer with CLI commands — the human has what they need at decision time.

---

### Lens 4 — LANDED→LEDGER→BASELINE-REFRESH CYCLE

**OBJECT on Type 5 (and partially Type 4) landing semantics.**

The M3 landing definition (§F): "'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch." Reconcile detects landing via merged PRs with `loop/` branch prefix in classdojo/iris. This works cleanly for Types 1, 2, 3 (prompt PR, habit PR, tool PR).

**Type 5 gap:** Type 5 candidates (routing/findings-pipeline code) route to an *ISSUE* in classdojo/iris, not a PR. A developer later implements the change with their own branch/PR (not a `loop/` branch). Reconcile never picks this up. Therefore:

- Type 5 approved candidates permanently sit in `approved-not-yet-landed`.
- The change-counter never increments for them.
- After 30 days the staleness alert fires — predictably and perpetually for every Type 5 route, creating noise that drowns out genuine staleness signals.
- The baseline-refresh trigger (change-counter = 5) is never reached by Type 5 approvals, regardless of how many code changes land.

DL-0023 §J defines "landed" for Type 2 specifically ("merged and approved") but says nothing about Type 5. DL-0023 §J's baseline refresh condition is "[5 tunable] approved candidates landed" — without restricting types. The M3 land definition silently excludes Type 5 from ever satisfying this condition.

**Type 4:** Type 4 (retrieval-corpus) is correctly excluded from the top-5 and surfaced only as BLIND-SPOT count lines — not approval candidates. No landing gap here.

**Recommended correction (two options, pick one):**
- **(a) Define a separate closed-loop path for Type 5:** Mark a Type 5 candidate as landed when its classdojo/iris issue is closed (check via `gh issue view <issue-number> --json state`), and increment the change-counter accordingly. This requires reconcile to also track open issues, not just merged PRs.
- **(b) Explicitly exclude Type 5 from the change-counter and acknowledge the staleness alert is expected:** Document that Type 5 entries must be manually closed in the ledger via `loop reject` once the developer implements them; the staleness alert for Type 5 items is a review prompt, not an error. Add a `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state distinct from `approved-not-yet-landed` so the alert reads correctly.

Option (b) is smaller and safer for v1.

---

### Lens 5 — DELTA-VS-BASELINE ATTRIBUTION

**AGREE — real signal, appropriately bounded.**

The regression detection is an actual re-eval measurement, not a heuristic. The ≤5-candidate batch granularity is a stated known limitation (DL-0023), not hand-waving — it's small enough for a human to bisect if needed. The rollback mechanism (revert the suspect classdojo/iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture) is concrete and executable. The CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner persistence (until rollback or explicit `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + rationale) prevents silent burial.

**Residual risk worth naming (non-blocking):** External IRIS commits (not from the loop) between the prior baseline IRIS commit and the refresh IRIS commit can cause regressions that look loop-caused. The baseline pointer tracks the pinned IRIS commit, so a human comparing the two commits can detect this — but the system doesn't surface the IRIS commit delta automatically at regression time. Recommend adding "IRIS SHA at prior baseline vs refresh baseline" to the CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner as a one-line diagnostic.

---

### Summary Table

| Lens | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 STATE | AGREE | Remove spurious dotdev query from reconcile |
| 2 IDEMPOTENCY | AGREE (same-day) / OBJECT (cross-day) | Add STALE-RUN warning for prior-day crashed runs |
| 3 REPORT | OBJECT | Clarify lifecycle: what `issue_posted` refers to; when route paths appear |
| 4 LANDED→LEDGER | OBJECT | Define landing semantics for Type 5; add `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state or issue-close check |
| 5 ATTRIBUTION | AGREE | Add IRIS commit delta to CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner (minor) |

**Questions blocking progress:**
1. Is `issue_posted` in the lifecycle a draft stub posted early, or is the full morning report issue posted at `emitted` time? (§B/§C coherence)
2. For Type 5 candidates: should "landed" be defined as issue-closed (requires reconcile to poll issues), or should Type 5 use a `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state that opts out of the automated landing path and staleness-alert semantics?

**Fix:** Add to §D or §E:
> "Routing executes immediately within the `loop approve` command after writing the approval record. The `routed` state update occurs before `loop approve` returns."

This also clarifies the two-phase crash-resume applies to the approve command, not a run phase.

---

**AGREE — other state corruption vectors handled**

- **Concurrent runs:** Single-operator + single-machine file lock (§A)
- **Hand-edited state:** SHA-256 checksum validation; REFUSE malformed/mismatched (§A)
- **Crash mid-route:** Two-phase write (§E) + crash-resume probe with `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --state open`
- **human_edited immutability:** "state edit BLOCKS changes to human_edited on existing entries" (§A)

**Pass** (assuming routing timing fix above).

---

### (3) WRONG-TARGET / BLAST

**AGREE — target validation exists, human-edited attribution isolated**

Evidence:
- §E: PATH-EXISTENCE VALIDATION via `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<resolved-path>?ref=<iris-commit>`; if missing → ROUTE-TARGET-STALE
- §E: Type-specific target configs (iris-prompt-targets.yaml, iris-habit-targets.yaml, iris-tool-targets.yaml)
- §D: `loop edit` writes `{original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}`
- §A: "human_edited:bool immutable" + edit BLOCKS changes on existing entries
- §G: "human-edited candidates included with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag" in regression attribution (excluded from net-attribution by the WORKED EXAMPLE "excluded from net-attribution")

A human-edited diff cannot silently re-enter clean attribution. The immutable flag and hash chain prevent tampering.

**Pass.**

---

### (4) SECRETS

**OBJECT — MEDIUM: Scrubbing pattern list is non-exhaustive**

The spec says (§H):
> "Secret-pattern scrubbing (sk-*, AKIA*, connection strings) on all LLM outputs before report/PR"

**Gap:** This covers OpenAI keys and AWS access keys but misses:
- Anthropic keys (`sk-ant-*`)
- GCP service account JSON blobs
- Database connection strings with embedded passwords (`postgres://user:pass@...`)
- Webhook URLs with tokens (`hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../...`)

**Fix:** Change to:
> "Secret-pattern scrubbing using a curated deny-list (sk-*, sk-ant-*, AKIA*, xoxb-*, postgres://, mysql://, mongodb://, hooks.slack.com, and any string matching `[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` adjacent to 'key', 'token', 'secret', or 'password') on all LLM outputs before report/PR."

Or reference an external secret-scanning pattern file that can be updated without spec revision.

---

**AGREE — other secret vectors handled**

- §H: "keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs"
- §H: Preflight error format: "'preflight failed: {service}', no usernames/hostnames/warehouse names"
- §H: "v1 operator local creds from env/secret store"

**Pass** (assuming pattern list expansion).

---

### (5) LOOP-HEALTH HALT

**AGREE — halt is strict and unbypassable**

Evidence from §C:
> "on FAILURE emit ONLY health + zero candidates (precedes candidate processing; no --force/--skip-health)"

The spec explicitly:
1. Orders health check BEFORE candidate processing
2. Prohibits `--force` or `--skip-health` flags
3. Emits "ONLY health + zero candidates" on failure

No bypass path exists.

**Pass.**

---

### (6) AUTO-MODE

**OBJECT — MEDIUM: `loop reconcile` auto-marks "landed" without re-approval**

The spec says (§F):
> "'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch (loop approve = human-approval event; GitHub merge = landing event; no second approval)"

This is intentional per the parenthetical, but consider: **a malicious actor with merge access to classdojo/iris could merge a loop/ branch PR without the original approver's knowledge**, and reconcile would auto-mark it landed.

**Risk:** This isn't auto-*approval* (the candidate was already approved), but it is auto-*landing* that bypasses any final review of what actually merged vs. what was approved.

**Mitigating evidence:** The spec records `merge entry {repo, sha}` and `diff hash` at approval. A post-hoc audit can compare them.

**Suggested hardening (LOW):** Add to §F:
> "Reconcile compares the merged PR's final diff hash against the approved diff hash; if mismatched (e.g., force-push after approval), mark as `landed_modified:true` and surface in the next report's LOOP-HEALTH section."

**Current state:** Not a blocker, but a defense-in-depth gap.

---

**AGREE — no auto-approval path**

- §I: "v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path"
- §D: "no batch-approve, no --auto-approve in v1"

**Pass.**

---

### LOW observations

**L1: File lock implementation unspecified**

§A says "single-machine file lock" but state lives on a git branch. Git doesn't provide file-level locking. Implementation needs an external lock (e.g., `flock` on a local sentinel file, or advisory lock via the GitHub API).

**L2: CLI atomicity under concurrent invocation**

If a user runs `loop approve A 1` and `loop reject A 1` from two terminals simultaneously, the spec doesn't define which wins. The file lock helps but the conflict resolution (last-write-wins? first-write-wins? error?) should be specified.

---

### Passes (sound with evidence)

| Aspect | Evidence |
|--------|----------|
| Default-reject fail-safe | §D: "no approval record by deadline = NOT routed" |
| Crash-resume for routing | §E: two-phase write + `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --state open` |
| State integrity | §A: SHA-256 checksum of canonicalized JSON; REFUSE malformed |
| human_edited immutability | §A: "BLOCKS changes to human_edited on existing entries" |
| Health halt strictness | §C: "no --force/--skip-health" |
| Path-existence validation | §E: `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<path>?ref=<commit>` |
| Reconcile dedup | §F: key = {repo, sha} + secondary candidate-id check |
| Staleness alert | §C.7: "N candidates approved >30d have not landed" |
| CI-failure runbook | §J: `loop reject` + let generator re-propose |

---

## Recommendation: **APPROVED WITH NOTES**

**Must address before implementation:**
1. **(HIGH)** Explicitly state that routing executes within `loop approve`, not as a deferred run phase. Without this, the spec contains a race condition between approve and reconcile.

**Should address:**
2. **(MEDIUM)** Expand secret scrubbing patterns or reference an external updatable pattern file.
3. **(MEDIUM)** Consider adding `landed_modified` detection for PRs that changed after approval.

**May defer:**
4. **(LOW)** Specify file lock mechanism and CLI conflict resolution.

---

## Decisions

1. **Routing timing judgment:** Interpreted the worked example as authoritative (routing is synchronous within `loop approve`). The spec body contradicts this by describing routing as a run lifecycle phase. Flagged as HIGH.

2. **Landed-without-re-approval:** Accepted as intentional per §F parenthetical, but flagged the defense-in-depth gap.

3. **Secret scrubbing scope:** Treated as MEDIUM rather than HIGH because scrubbing is defense-in-depth; primary control is "keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs" which relies on code paths, not pattern matching.

4. **Deferred inspection:** Did not inspect classdojo/iris repo structure or existing target config files (OD-1/2/3 are explicitly marked OPEN and non-blocking for design).

APPROVAL GATE (CLI, per-candidate): `loop approve <date> <id>` writes {authenticated operator identity, ts, exact diff hash}; fails APPROVAL-DEADLINE-EXPIRED if a newer run key exists. `loop reject <date> <id>` writes explicit rejection (also valid to close a stale approved-not-yet-landed entry). `loop edit <date> <id>` opens the diff in $EDITOR; on save validate + rehash, write {original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}, then REQUIRE a separate `loop approve`. DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by deadline = NOT routed (no rubber-stamp by omission, no batch-approve, no --auto-approve in v1). ROUTING DEADLINE: a candidate is implicitly rejected when the NEXT `loop run` completes reconcile (aligns with daily cadence; cannot approve after a new run starts).

PATH-EXISTENCE VALIDATION for Types 1/2/3: `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<resolved-path>?ref=<iris-commit>`; if missing, abort ROUTE-TARGET-STALE before two-phase. Write the artifact URL to state before advancing. Type 1 prompt/instruction → PR into classdojo/iris at the path from loop/config/iris-prompt-targets.yaml ({sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→paths), branch loop/<date>-<id>, body = hypothesis + confounder card + report link + [HUMAN-EDITED] if applicable. Type 2 reflection/habit → PR into iris (v1 PR-only, no direct store write), scoped {scope, scope_key}, path from iris-habit-targets.yaml (OD-2 must resolve first, else ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2). Type 4 retrieval-corpus → NOT auto-PR'd; human-judgment ISSUE in classdojo/iris (EVAL-INVISIBLE). 'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch (loop approve = human-approval event; GitHub merge = landing event; no second approval). G. PROVENANCE: at each refresh, the DL-0023 §J delta-vs-last-baseline check attributes per-case regressions to the batch of ≤5 landed candidates since the last refresh (batch granularity, known limitation); human-edited candidates included with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag. H. SECRETS / ACCESS: scoring needs warehouse creds + LLM keys (--execute --e2e). v1 operator local creds from env/secret store; keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs. Secret-pattern scrubbing (sk-*, AKIA*, connection strings) on all LLM outputs before report/PR. [OPEN: local vs CI runner].

I. AUTO MODE (deferred, slice 6): v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path until a multi-run track record + trusted sentinel/health.

RECOVERY RUNBOOK — LOOP PR FAILS IRIS CI: run `loop reject <date> <id>` (writes explicit rejection, clears the approved-not-yet-landed entry, lets the next run's generator re-cluster from the same failure class if it persists). SPECIALIST REVIEWS:
### [1/3] critic

## Critique

**Summary:** The proposal is substantially sound — all 14 round-2 fixes check out, and the core state, idempotency, and attribution mechanics are coherent. Two concrete design contradictions need resolution before implementation can safely start.

---

### Lens 1 — STATE MODEL

**AGREE, with one minor flag.**

- Single source of truth (loop/state.json on loop-state), SHA-256 guard, `REFUSE` on mismatch, and `human_edited` immutable — correct.
- Dedup on `{repo, sha}` with secondary candidate-id warning prevents double-landing.
- Change-counter increments per merged PR; quarantine clocks advance only at `emitted` — these are correctly decoupled.
- Preflight `gh api repos/johnalexwelch/dotdev/rulesets` correctly confirms loop-state is not covered by the DL-0011 main-only ruleset.

**Flag (non-blocking):** Reconcile queries "merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix `loop/`." No `loop/` PRs merge into dotdev's main — all routes go to classdojo/iris (Types 1–3 as PRs; Types 4–5 as issues). The dotdev query is spurious. It adds confusion without risk. Recommend removing it or documenting explicitly why it's there (e.g. future expansion).

---

### Lens 2 — IDEMPOTENCY / CRASH-RESUME

**AGREE for same-day crashes. OBJECT for cross-day crashes.**

Same-key crash-resume is correct: write `status=routing` before creation, probe `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --state open` before recreating, write URL before advancing. Within the same date the scheme is sound.

**Concrete gap:** The run key includes `date`. If a run crashes at `status=routed` and the operator resumes the *next* day, the new date produces a new run key. The new run's reconcile picks up only MERGED PRs with `loop/` prefix — but the prior day's PRs may still be open (approved, created, not yet reviewed/merged). The crash-resume probe is never invoked for the old key. Those open PRs are opaque to the new run: the operator sees them in classdojo/iris but the loop doesn't surface them, track their approval status, or warn about the dangling state. They'll eventually merge and reconcile will pick them up correctly (`{repo, sha}` dedup prevents double-landing), but until then the state shows them as approved-not-yet-landed for the old run and the new run has no visibility that the old run was never emitted.

**Recommended correction (small):** Add a `STALE-RUN` check to the start of every new run: if any run exists in state with `status ≠ emitted` and a run key ≠ today's, surface a warning listing the stale run key and its routed-but-open PR URLs. No action required — just visibility.

---

### Lens 3 — REPORT DECISION-COMPLETENESS

**OBJECT on lifecycle ordering contradiction.**

The report (§C.3) requires "fully-resolved route path" for each candidate — actual PR/issue URLs in classdojo/iris. These URLs only exist after routing completes. But the run lifecycle is: `started → issue_posted:{url} → routed:{ids, pr_urls} → emitted`. The morning report issue is posted *before* routing. This is internally contradictory: you cannot show a fully-resolved route path in a report posted before routing runs.

This is not a nitpick. Different implementers would resolve it differently:
- Post the issue early with placeholder paths, then edit it after routing — adds an implicit "issue edit" step not in the spec.
- Post the issue at `emitted` time (after routing) — consistent with report content, but then `issue_posted` isn't a distinct lifecycle step.
- `issue_posted` refers to a separate tracking/kickoff issue (not the morning report), and the morning report is committed at `emitted` — plausible, but not stated.

**Recommended correction:** Clarify that `issue_posted` in the lifecycle refers to a lightweight run-tracking stub (just "run started, report will be here"), posted early so the operator has a URL to watch. The full morning report (including route paths) is written at `emitted` time — committed to `loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` on loop-state *and* posted as an edit/update to the stub issue, or as a separate issue posted at emit. The spec should state which.

All other report content checks pass: header, sentinel PASS/HALT, confounder card per candidate (permutation p, FDR q, blast tier, cross-lane note, flags), HIGH-blast callout, CANNOT-VALIDATE separation, fixture-gap backlog status, staleness alert, cumulative-regression banner, footer with CLI commands — the human has what they need at decision time.

---

### Lens 4 — LANDED→LEDGER→BASELINE-REFRESH CYCLE

**OBJECT on Type 5 (and partially Type 4) landing semantics.**

The M3 landing definition (§F): "'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch." Reconcile detects landing via merged PRs with `loop/` branch prefix in classdojo/iris. This works cleanly for Types 1, 2, 3 (prompt PR, habit PR, tool PR).

**Type 5 gap:** Type 5 candidates (routing/findings-pipeline code) route to an *ISSUE* in classdojo/iris, not a PR. A developer later implements the change with their own branch/PR (not a `loop/` branch). Reconcile never picks this up. Therefore:

- Type 5 approved candidates permanently sit in `approved-not-yet-landed`.
- The change-counter never increments for them.
- After 30 days the staleness alert fires — predictably and perpetually for every Type 5 route, creating noise that drowns out genuine staleness signals.
- The baseline-refresh trigger (change-counter = 5) is never reached by Type 5 approvals, regardless of how many code changes land.

DL-0023 §J defines "landed" for Type 2 specifically ("merged and approved") but says nothing about Type 5. DL-0023 §J's baseline refresh condition is "[5 tunable] approved candidates landed" — without restricting types. The M3 land definition silently excludes Type 5 from ever satisfying this condition.

**Type 4:** Type 4 (retrieval-corpus) is correctly excluded from the top-5 and surfaced only as BLIND-SPOT count lines — not approval candidates. No landing gap here.

**Recommended correction (two options, pick one):**
- **(a) Define a separate closed-loop path for Type 5:** Mark a Type 5 candidate as landed when its classdojo/iris issue is closed (check via `gh issue view <issue-number> --json state`), and increment the change-counter accordingly. This requires reconcile to also track open issues, not just merged PRs.
- **(b) Explicitly exclude Type 5 from the change-counter and acknowledge the staleness alert is expected:** Document that Type 5 entries must be manually closed in the ledger via `loop reject` once the developer implements them; the staleness alert for Type 5 items is a review prompt, not an error. Add a `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state distinct from `approved-not-yet-landed` so the alert reads correctly.

Option (b) is smaller and safer for v1.

---

### Lens 5 — DELTA-VS-BASELINE ATTRIBUTION

**AGREE — real signal, appropriately bounded.**

The regression detection is an actual re-eval measurement, not a heuristic. The ≤5-candidate batch granularity is a stated known limitation (DL-0023), not hand-waving — it's small enough for a human to bisect if needed. The rollback mechanism (revert the suspect classdojo/iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture) is concrete and executable. The CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner persistence (until rollback or explicit `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + rationale) prevents silent burial.

**Residual risk worth naming (non-blocking):** External IRIS commits (not from the loop) between the prior baseline IRIS commit and the refresh IRIS commit can cause regressions that look loop-caused. The baseline pointer tracks the pinned IRIS commit, so a human comparing the two commits can detect this — but the system doesn't surface the IRIS commit delta automatically at regression time. Recommend adding "IRIS SHA at prior baseline vs refresh baseline" to the CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner as a one-line diagnostic.

---

### Summary Table

| Lens | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 STATE | AGREE | Remove spurious dotdev query from reconcile |
| 2 IDEMPOTENCY | AGREE (same-day) / OBJECT (cross-day) | Add STALE-RUN warning for prior-day crashed runs |
| 3 REPORT | OBJECT | Clarify lifecycle: what `issue_posted` refers to; when route paths appear |
| 4 LANDED→LEDGER | OBJECT | Define landing semantics for Type 5; add `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state or issue-close check |
| 5 ATTRIBUTION | AGREE | Add IRIS commit delta to CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner (minor) |

**Questions blocking progress:**
1. Is `issue_posted` in the lifecycle a draft stub posted early, or is the full morning report issue posted at `emitted` time? (§B/§C coherence)
2. For Type 5 candidates: should "landed" be defined as issue-closed (requires reconcile to poll issues), or should Type 5 use a `PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION` state that opts out of the automated landing path and staleness-alert semantics?

---

### [2/3] analyst

## Analysis

**Reviewing through the four judge lenses only.** I did a targeted check of the generator design (`iris-loop-candidate-generator-v1.md`) and decision log to verify cross-references before rendering verdicts.

---

### Lens 1 — Route targets map to actual IRIS surfaces

**Type 1 (prompt/instruction → PR into iris):** AGREE. Path-existence validation via `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<path>?ref=<iris-commit>` before two-phase commit ensures the PR targets a real file at a known commit. ROUTE-TARGET-STALE aborts cleanly if the path has moved. The three path buckets (sql_generation, findings_prose, system_prefix) in iris-prompt-targets.yaml align with the real IRIS surfaces DL-0021 identified.

**Type 2 (reflection/habit → PR into iris):** AGREE, conditional on OD-2. "v1 PR-only, no direct store write" is the right conservative call — avoids an out-of-band write to a store whose path is unresolved. ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2 correctly blocks routing without blocking the rest of the design.

**Type 3 (tool schema → PR into iris):** AGREE. The `{target_tool_path}` field + iris-tool-targets.yaml requirement is the right guard — without it, a schema candidate has nowhere to land.

**Type 4 (retrieval-corpus → ISSUE in iris, EVAL-INVISIBLE):** AGREE on the routing artifact itself. Creating an issue rather than a PR is correct — a retrieval-corpus change bypasses the eval entirely and needs human judgment before any file changes. The EVAL-INVISIBLE note in the report's blind-spot section (§C.6) is the right visibility surface.

**Type 5 (routing/findings-pipeline code → ISSUE in iris):** AGREE on routing artifact. Code changes need a human implementation step; an issue is the right lightweight handoff.

---

### Lens 2 — Cross-repo routing actually lands in the right place

**PR-based types (1/2/3):** AGREE. `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo <target>` crash-resume probe, two-phase state write, and the reconcile step (filtering `base:default-branch` + `branch prefix loop/`) form a coherent chain. State writes occur before artifact creation; idempotency on resume is clean.

**OBJECT — Issue-based types (4/5 and fixture-gap) have no landing-detection mechanism, and this is a blocking design hole.**

§F reconcile reads: *"Queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix loop/ AND base:default-branch."* GitHub issues are not PRs. They do not have a merge event. A Type 4 or Type 5 item, once approved and routed (issue created), will **never be detected as landed by reconcile**. Consequences that break the design end-to-end:

1. The item permanently sits in `approved-not-yet-landed`. The §C.7 staleness alert fires after 30 days and never clears — becoming alarm fatigue rather than a real signal.
2. The change-counter never increments for issue-routed approvals. A batch of five approvals that are all Type 4/5 will never trigger a baseline-refresh proposal (§F), silently stalling the loop's improvement cycle.
3. §G regression attribution omits Type 4/5 from the suspect batch. If a Type 4 retrieval-corpus change degrades the agent, the provenance chain is broken.
